body: Several factors affect what you pay in Azure: the resource type, consumption, maintenance, geography, subscription type, and Azure Marketplace purchases. Geography matters because the same resource can cost different amounts in different regions. To lower cost you can use reservations, committing to specific resources for one or three years, or an Azure savings plan for compute, committing to an hourly spend for one or three years. Azure Spot Virtual Machines use unused capacity at lower prices for workloads that can be interrupted.
author: claude

body: The Azure pricing calculator estimates what Azure resources will cost before you deploy anything. You can price individual resources, build a full solution, or start from an example scenario. It covers compute, storage and network costs, and lets you account for storage type, access tier and redundancy, so you can compare estimates across regions and service tiers. It is for information only. Nothing is provisioned when you add resources to it, and you are not charged.
author: claude

body: Tags are metadata about your resources. A tag has a name and a value, such as CostCenter with a cost center code, and you can add one or more tags to each resource. Tags let you group resources to report on costs, allocate internal cost centers, track budgets and forecast cost. Resources do not inherit tags from their subscription or resource group, so tag each resource you want to report on. Azure Policy can require tags on new resources.
author: claude
